simple.meaning: אֵלוֹן (ʼêlôwn) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an oak or other strong tree.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Genesis 12:6. The surrounding context includes family, altar, Torah, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to אֵלוֹן (H436) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

timeline.evidenceText: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time, Canaanites were in the land.
Abram moved his tent, and came and lived by the oaks of Mamre, which are in Hebron, and built an altar there to Yahweh.
One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. They were allies of Abram.
Yahweh appeared to him by the oaks of Mamre, as he sat in the tent door in the heat of the day.
Aren’t they beyond the Jordan, behind the way of the going down of the sun, in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the Arabah near Gilgal, beside the oaks of Moreh?
Now Heber the Kenite had separated himself from the Kenites, even from the children of Hobab, Moses’ brother-in-law, and had pitched his tent as far as the oak in Zaanannim, which is by Kedesh.
All the men of Shechem assembled themselves together with all the house of Millo, and went and made Abimelech king by the oak of the pillar that was in Shechem.
Gaal spoke again and said, “Behold, people are coming down by the middle of the land, and one company comes by the way of the oak of Meonenim.”

“Then you will go on forward from there, and you will come to the oak of Tabor. Three men will meet you there going up to God to Bethel, one carrying three young goats, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a container of wine.

definitions.short: an oak or other strong tree
definitions.full: H436. elon I. אֵלוֺן noun [feminine] terebinth (= אֵלָה ) — ׳א construct Gen 12:6 4 t.; plural construct אֵלוֺנֵי 13:18 3 t. — terebinth (or other tall tree, compare below on 1Sam 10:3 ; Judg 4:5 ), marking shrine, & hence used in topographic designations; ׳א מוֺרֶה ( teacher's terebinth ) Gen 12:6 (see Di) so Deut 11:30 ; ׳א מְעוֺנְנִים ( eonjurors' tereb. ) Judg 9:37 ; distinguished by owner or ruler ׳א מַמְרֵא Gen 13:18 ; 14:13 ; 18:1 ; by neighbouring town (ב)צענים Judg 4:11 ; compare ׳א בְּצַעֲנַנִּים Josh 19:33 (editions אַלּוֺן , but see Norzi Baer Di.); ׳אֵ בִּשְׁכֶם אֲשֶׁר מֻצָּב Judg 9:6 (compare אֵלָה Gen 35:4 ); ׳א תָּבוֺר 1Sam 10:3 read ׳א דְּבוֺרָה (& compare בָּכוּת אַלּוֺן Gen 35:8 , & דְּבוֺרָה תֹּמֶר Judg 4:5 ) compare Ew Geschichte iii. 31 Th Di Gen 35:8 (see also below אַלּוֺן ).
